concepts.name: Definition and Core Formula of GDP Deflator
key_dimensions: Formula: (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 — and what each component represents
Why it is expressed as an index number, not a percentage rate directly
Distinction between GDP deflator as a price index vs. an inflation measure
Common UPSC trap: confusing GDP deflator value with inflation rate

concepts.name: GDP Deflator vs. Consumer Price Index (CPI): Conceptual Differences
key_dimensions: Coverage: GDP deflator covers all domestically produced goods & services; CPI covers a fixed consumer basket
Treatment of imports: CPI includes imported goods, GDP deflator excludes them
Base year fixed basket (CPI/WPI) vs. changing basket (GDP deflator — Paasche index)
Which is a better measure of economy-wide inflation and why — UPSC favourite comparison

concepts.name: GDP Deflator vs. Wholesale Price Index (WPI): Key Distinctions
key_dimensions: WPI covers only goods (no services); GDP deflator covers goods and services
WPI uses a fixed base-year Laspeyres index; GDP deflator uses current-year weights (Paasche)
WPI excludes investment goods and government services; GDP deflator includes them
Practical implication: WPI and GDP deflator can move in opposite directions — UPSC trap

concepts.name: Paasche Price Index Nature of GDP Deflator
key_dimensions: Definition of Paasche index: uses current-year quantities as weights
Contrast with Laspeyres index (base-year weights) used in CPI/WPI
Implication: GDP deflator tends to understate inflation (substitution bias direction opposite to CPI)
Why the basket changes every year — automatic updating without explicit revision

concepts.name: Nominal GDP vs. Real GDP: The Deflation Mechanism
key_dimensions: Nominal GDP: valued at current-year prices; Real GDP: valued at base-year prices
How GDP deflator is used to convert nominal to real GDP (deflating process)
Base year selection and its policy implications in India (current base year: 2011-12)
UPSC trap: if GDP deflator > 100, real GDP < nominal GDP, and vice versa

concepts.name: GDP Deflator and Measurement of Inflation
key_dimensions: GDP deflator inflation rate = % change in GDP deflator between two periods
Why RBI/government prefers CPI for monetary policy over GDP deflator
GDP deflator as a broader but less timely inflation signal
Scenario-based trap: economy with rising services prices — GDP deflator rises even if WPI is stable

concepts.name: Scope and Coverage: What GDP Deflator Includes and Excludes
key_dimensions: Includes: private consumption, government expenditure, gross capital formation, net exports (production side)
Excludes: imported goods (critical UPSC distinction from CPI)
Includes investment goods (machinery, construction) — unlike CPI
Covers informal sector output if captured in GDP estimates — broader than any single price index

concepts.name: GDP Deflator and India's National Income Estimation (CSO/MOSPI)
key_dimensions: Role of National Statistical Office (NSO/MOSPI) in computing GDP deflator
Data sources used: WPI, CPI, producer price indices for different sectors
Implicit vs. explicit deflators — GDP deflator is an implicit price deflator
Frequency: available only annually (quarterly with lag), unlike monthly CPI/WPI — policy limitation

concepts.name: Implicit Price Deflator Concept
key_dimensions: GDP deflator is called an 'implicit' deflator because it is derived, not directly surveyed
Derived implicitly from the ratio of nominal to real GDP estimates
Contrast with explicit price indices (CPI, WPI) based on direct price surveys
UPSC trap: 'implicit' does not mean 'approximate' — it is a precise mathematical derivation

concepts.name: GDP Deflator and Sectoral Deflators in India
key_dimensions: Different deflators used for different sectors: WPI for manufacturing, CPI-AL for agriculture, etc.
Composite GDP deflator is a weighted average of sectoral deflators
When sectoral composition of GDP shifts (e.g., services boom), overall deflator changes
Policy implication: a services-dominated economy may show low WPI but high GDP deflator

concepts.name: Base Year Revision and Its Impact on GDP Deflator
key_dimensions: India's base year revisions: 1999-2000 → 2004-05 → 2011-12 (current)
Revision changes the reference point, altering both real GDP and deflator values
Why base year revision is necessary: structural changes in the economy
UPSC trap: after base revision, historical real GDP and deflator figures are restated — data inconsistency

concepts.name: GDP Deflator When Inflation is Negative (Deflation Scenario)
key_dimensions: GDP deflator < 100 implies price levels have fallen below base year — deflation
Real GDP > Nominal GDP in deflation scenario — UPSC numerical trap
India's experience: GDP deflator has occasionally been very low (near deflation) in commodity price crash years
Policy implication: deflation raises real debt burden; GDP deflator signals this before CPI does for producers

concepts.name: GDP Deflator and Purchasing Power / Standard of Living Analysis
key_dimensions: Real GDP per capita (deflated by GDP deflator) as a standard of living proxy
Why using nominal GDP per capita without deflation overstates welfare improvements
International comparisons: PPP-adjusted GDP vs. GDP deflator-adjusted real GDP — different purposes
UPSC linkage: HDI uses GNI per capita in PPP terms, not directly GDP deflator

concepts.name: GDP Deflator vs. GNP/GNI Deflator
key_dimensions: GDP deflator based on domestic production; GNP deflator also accounts for net factor income from abroad
For India: GNP slightly less than GDP (net factor income is marginally negative)
Deflating GNP requires adjusting for price changes in foreign income flows
UPSC trap: GDP deflator ≠ GNP deflator — distinction matters when net factor income is significant

concepts.name: Relationship Between GDP Deflator and Terms of Trade
key_dimensions: Terms of trade = export price index / import price index
Since imports are excluded from GDP deflator, a rise in import prices does NOT raise GDP deflator
But rising import prices raise CPI — causing GDP deflator and CPI to diverge
Policy trap: oil price shock raises CPI/WPI inflation but may not show up strongly in GDP deflator

concepts.name: GDP Deflator in the Context of Fiscal Policy Assessment
key_dimensions: Nominal fiscal deficit vs. real fiscal deficit: GDP deflator used to assess real burden
Inflation (GDP deflator) erodes real value of government debt — 'inflation tax' concept
Real interest rate = nominal rate minus GDP deflator inflation — affects real cost of borrowing
UPSC application: assessing whether rising nominal GDP growth is real or price-driven

concepts.name: GDP Deflator and Economic Growth Decomposition
key_dimensions: Nominal GDP growth = Real GDP growth + GDP deflator inflation (approximately)
Decomposing headline GDP growth into volume effect vs. price effect
UPSC trap: high nominal GDP growth with high deflator inflation may mean low real growth
India context: years of high nominal growth masking moderate real growth due to high deflation

concepts.name: Limitations of GDP Deflator as a Policy Tool
key_dimensions: Not available monthly — delayed availability makes it unsuitable for real-time monetary policy
Covers only market-produced GDP — misses black economy, non-market household production
Paasche index underestimates inflation when consumers substitute away from expensive goods
Does not capture quality changes in goods and services (quality bias)

concepts.name: GDP Deflator in Comparing Across Countries (International Context)
key_dimensions: Each country has its own GDP deflator; not directly comparable across nations
World Bank and IMF use country-specific GDP deflators for real growth comparisons
PPP conversion factors are conceptually different from GDP deflators — UPSC confusion point
IMF World Economic Outlook uses GDP deflator to compute real GDP growth rates for member countries

concepts.name: Numerical Interpretation and Exam-Oriented Calculations of GDP Deflator
key_dimensions: Given nominal GDP and real GDP, compute deflator and interpret whether prices rose or fell
Given GDP deflator and nominal GDP, compute real GDP — standard UPSC prelims numerical
Identifying which year is the base year (deflator = 100) from a data table
UPSC trap: GDP deflator of 110 means prices rose 10% from base year, NOT 110% — common error
